programme: A TGF-β/Smad–NF-κB signaling node: SMAD6 (an inhibitory Smad) and KLF11 (which transcriptionally targets SMAD3 and SMAD7) set TGF-β/BMP pathway tone, while NKRF and KLF2 constrain NF-κB-driven inflammatory output; PHF20 couples this to p53 stabilization and chromatin readout, and LMO4 executes a CREB-repressive transcriptional consequence downstream.
role_in_a: In Alzheimer's disease this axis is documented piecemeal as part of reactive neuroinflammatory and synaptic-loss signaling: SMAD6 appears in TGF-β-linked T-helper-9 differentiation changes and is a miR-106b target in a transgenic AD model, NKRF is tied to dysregulated NF-κB signaling in AD transcriptomic studies, KLF2 is reported as a miR-25 target whose loss aggravates Aβ-induced hippocampal neuron injury, and LMO4 has the strongest direct support — as a CSF synaptic biomarker and as a CREB corepressor implicated in Aβ-induced synapse loss.
role_in_b: In Lower Grade Glioma the same module is repurposed for glial growth: nuclear SMAD6 sequesters PIAS3 away from STAT3, relieving STAT3 repression and directly promoting gliomagenesis (documented), and PHF20 drives a WISP1/BGN-dependent pathway that promotes glioblastoma cell malignancy (documented). KLF11's transcriptional link to SMAD3/SMAD7 places TGF-β pathway tone — a recognized immunosuppressive/growth axis in glioma — alongside these, though no glioma-specific paper was retrieved for KLF11, NKRF, or KLF2.
shared_axis: Both are brain-tissue conditions built on glial reactivity — astrocyte/microglial activation in AD, tumor-glia proliferation in LGG — and TGF-β/Smad and NF-κB signaling are the canonical controllers of that reactive state in both contexts. The same node (SMAD6-gated Smad/STAT3 balance, NKRF/KLF2-gated NF-κB tone) could plausibly be held in a restrained, homeostatic configuration in healthy glia and become dysregulated in disease-specific but mechanistically related ways — chronic low-grade activation in AD, disinhibited proliferative activation in glioma.
reasoning: The module is nameable from the factors themselves and both diseases have independent literature placing distinct members of it — SMAD6 is in fact the one factor with direct evidence in both AD (TGF-β/Th9, miR-106b) and LGG (PIAS3-STAT3 de-repression) — but no retrieved paper states the AD–LGG connection itself; that link is inferred from shared tissue and shared pathway biology rather than found. That keeps this at supported/moderate rather than established/strong.
support: PMID 29950561 shows nuclear SMAD6 promotes gliomagenesis by blocking PIAS3-mediated STAT3 inhibition; PMID 38935935 and PMID 20709030 place SMAD6/TGF-β pathway changes in Alzheimer's disease models; PMID 33117706 shows PHF20 drives glioblastoma malignancy via WISP1/BGN; PMID 38738952 places NKRF in NF-κB dysregulation in Alzheimer's disease; PMID 31144355 places KLF2 downstream of miR-25 in Aβ-induced neuronal injury; PMID 40105503, PMID 36594364, and PMID 14720177 place LMO4 in Alzheimer's synaptic pathology and CREB-mediated Aβ synapse loss.
how_to_falsify: In reactive astrocytes/microglia from an AD model, knock down or overexpress SMAD6 and test whether it alters nuclear PIAS3-STAT3 association and NKRF/KLF2-dependent NF-κB target gene expression the way it does in glioma cells; if SMAD6 does not relieve STAT3 repression or shift NF-κB output in AD-relevant glia the way it does in LGG cells, the proposed shared mechanism is wrong and the overlap is coincidental co-recurrence rather than a reused signaling node.
caveats: Both diseases share tissue (brain|brain), so any glial-signaling overlap is anatomically unsurprising rather than a novel pairing. 248 patient-group comparisons across 6 independent cohort pairs is a substantial base, but the carrying factors are each concordant in only ~87-97/248 (35-39%) of groups — moderate, not near-universal, agreement. PGR (126/248) and MNT (119/248) have higher raw recurrence than any carrying factor but were excluded from the programme because no retrieved literature ties either to a coherent mechanism in this pairing and their target sets (canonical steroid-response genes for PGR; MYC-MAX network genes for MNT) point to different, unconnected biology. SOX10 and NOTCH1 were removed as tissue-generic, so this account deliberately does not reach for the obvious glial master regulators. HOXD8, NRL, ATOH7, and SPDEF are concordant but retina-developmental or epithelial in character with no retrieved evidence for either disease, and were left out rather than forced into the story.
